predictions.text: Def book in the city. Otherwise you’re literally wasting let’s say you only go into the city 4 times - 10.6+ hours of your trip just sitting in public transport.
There are pedicab tours in Central Park that take you to movie locations. Or you can walk it. Might be far for the kinder.

Lived for years in New Haven, about the same distance out, and would train in and out same day on occasion. Then I moved to Manhattan for several years. The experience will be different. If you stay in the City you see the full daily rhythm--for example, when shows end at 10 you go to a rooftop bar, not to the train. Also, as a tourist it is damned difficult to find a place to just sit down for a break, much less find a clean restroom (my wife adds), so having a hotel nearby for a break is huge. And next month it will be cold, could be rainy too, so you will want to warm up and dry.

1) The daily LIRR transportation prices will probably be what we locals pay per week, per person. 2) That and if you miss the LIRR/suburban lines, you typically have to wait much much longer, and some lines don’t even run at night/off-peak so you risk getting stranded. 3) The daily time commitment is hefty. 

NY State transportation system (like LIRR) is different, suburban based, and more expensive, from the NY City transportation system (OMNY) which is cheaper, local, city based. So if you have to additionally use the LIRR/suburban line. you’ll pay much, much, more per day for transportation to commute to/from the NYS suburbs, and the prices additionally add up since you’ll need to pay for both local city transportation, and suburban transportation so it adds up. 

Local OMNY-NYC transportation has a weekly cap on fares I think it’s $36 max per person after which all rides are free (12 rides x$3 each) so that’s more economical. 

Get a cheap hotel within a few miles of the city center and you’ll be fine. You’ll likely spend little time in a hotel when visiting and touring.
One thing: this includes A LOT of outside activities and there is a possibility the weather will be brutal. You might want to plan accordingly.

Is it one hour and 20 minutes each way, or is that your total commute time? One thing I know about running around New York City is that I really like to have someplace during the day to retreat - even for 30 minutes - put my feet up maybe even take a little nap before heading back out again. 

If you're going to do this, before you head out each day, take a good look at your destination for the day for some NEARBY very comfortable coffee shops to sit down and put your feet up. Coffee shops tend to be less hectic than bars.

Bonus of the coffee shop has sofas.

Everyone's saying "oh i make that commute every day," but we're not talking about a daily work commute, we're talking about a first time tourist. If I were to visit a city for the first time and want to explore and pack my day (and night, it sounds like), there's no way I'd want to start and end each day with an hour and a half train ride. I expect you will be exhausted and it'll make you grumpy, or by midweek you'll be burned out and just wanna stay on long island. Which is fine, but not what you are coming here for.

Halal Guys is a chain. You can get them in Las Vegas, for example. Also, your Friday is bonkers. Harlem to the UN to Brooklyn is SO much transit. And Harlem deserves more time, frankly. Time Out Market is swamped all the time and I wouldn’t recommend it unless you want to wade through crowds and eat standing up. I also wouldn’t eat in Little Italy. Do your Chinatown research because some places are still legit but others are tourist traps. I don’t eat much Chinese food so can’t make personal recommendations. Also please don’t eat a cart hot dog, especially if you can go to Gray’s Papaya instead. Get a pretzel (or even better, chestnuts if you find them) if you must order from a street cart.

Sunday the theatre and museum?  And steak house?    
Monday Washington Square and cruise?  How long is the cruise?  Saturday are you just touring Carnegie Hall?  10 years old he should be able to keep up.  Rest stations and water/snacks enjoy.

for you i highly suggest you make time to visit the museum at fit -- its free. afterwards you can walk east on w26st as given the fashion students there are a number of thrift stores along the way. from there you are in nomad/madison park.
How are you planning to travel from the UN to dumbo? I would suggest taking the east river ferry from east 34 st. Here’s the schedule https://www.ferry.nyc/routes-and-schedules/east-river/

I’d consider staying with the cousin if you were just going in for a game or show or something, but it all 6 days are meant to be in the city, stay in the city. The amount you’ll spend on round trip LIRR tickets or parking is already like 1/3-1/2 of a hotel price.
I’d stay in the city so you can feel more immersed in it.
If you can afford a hotel, stay in one. If you can't/don't want to, then stay with the cuz. or maybe a mixture of the 2. Clearly, it's going to take 3 hours out of your day to commute. Your choice.

That sounds annoying, just spend the money on a hotel. What if you’re out buying stuff and want to drop it off at the hotel midday? Or want to freshen up before a meal? Can’t do that if you’re staying with them.

Time is money when you travel! Stay where you want to visit. And while the offer of a free place to stay is nice, it’s a bit tone deaf to suggest first time visitors want to use their limited time to commute 3 hours round trip. And the travel time will certainly be longer than that. As others have pointed out, the commuting time has to include getting to/from the LIRR station on each end, choosing local trains (either by accident or bc it’s the only option) and being bound to the train schedule.  None of that is fodder for vacation.

I wouldn’t. LIRR trains don’t run as frequently as the trains in the city and you’d have to schedule it out, it sounds like a lot to do every day. I’d do a couple nights in the city and maybe a couple nights with them on the days you want to do Queens and Brooklyn (which you should do, don’t only see Manhattan).
